items.title: Mayor-Elect Tedjo Joins Ford to Open Ontario's Largest Grocery Store in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Now Toronto, Food World Plus opened to shoppers on Oct. 30 at 50 Matheson Blvd. East, becoming Ontario's largest grocery store at 176,000 square feet. The outlet reported the store centers its selling point on global food, stocking products from the Mediterranean, Latin America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Now Toronto said the store aims to save Mississauga's diverse population from visiting multiple specialty grocers for hard to find ingredients. Beyond groceries, the store includes a flower section, bakery, deli, fresh meat department and an in house butcher, according to the outlet. Mayor elect Alvin Tedjo attended the grand opening alongside Ontario Premier Doug Ford, Now Toronto reported. The outlet noted the meat department includes a dedicated halal section, with meat sourced from a certified halal supplier and handled according to halal standards.

items.title: Extra Daily Math and Literacy Time Lifts EQAO Scores at Toronto and Peel Schools
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star, a Toronto elementary school and a Mississauga school in the Peel District School Board dramatically improved their EQAO test scores, and the newspaper drew lessons from both. The outlet detailed Corvette Junior Public School in Scarborough, where a balanced day schedule gives students 100 minutes of uninterrupted math daily, 40 more than the province requires, plus 100 minutes for literacy. The Star reported the extra math time allows for longer lessons and group work that help teachers identify struggling students. In one example, Grade 5 and 6 students worked in small groups on a word problem, writing equations and checking answers with addition. A student identified as Shaun told the Star that math is fun even when it is challenging. The newspaper said similar lessons were drawn from Mississauga's Brian W. Fleming school within the Peel board.

items.title: Felician Sisters Weigh Next Step for Shuttered Mississauga Catholic School After Farewell Mass
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto, hundreds of alumnae and staff gathered Saturday for a final mass marking the end of their former Catholic high school. The gathering closed out Holy Name of Mary College School, a Mississauga institution that shut its doors in June. CBC reported the school closed due to low enrolment. The 62 year old building's future remains uncertain, the broadcaster said. Its owners, the Felician Sisters of St. Francis, have not yet decided what will happen to the property, according to CBC.

items.title: Toronto Police Name Two Suspects, Including a Teen, in Fatal Etobicoke Shooting of Mississauga Man
items.summary: According to insauga.com, Toronto police have issued Canada-wide warrants for two suspects in the fatal shooting of an 18-year-old Mississauga man in Etobicoke on Nov. 7. Officers found the victim with gunshot wounds and attempted life-saving measures before paramedics took him to hospital, where he later died, insauga.com reported. The suspects fled before police arrived. In an update issued Saturday, police said they identified Armani Callender, 19, and Cameron Marlor, 17, both of Toronto, as wanted on Canada-wide warrants, according to the outlet. Police said they obtained a judge's permission to publicly name Marlor despite his age, an order that expires at noon on Thursday, Nov. 19, insauga.com reported. Investigators have released images of both suspects. Police have not said which charges relate to which suspect, or whether anyone else was hurt, according to the outlet.

items.title: Mississauga Could Delay Opening Four Outdoor Rinks as El Nino Threatens a Milder Winter
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, a forecasted strong El Nino weather pattern could disrupt municipal services this fall and winter, including delays opening outdoor skating rinks. The city said El Nino is a natural global pattern that recurs every two to seven years, marked by warmer than average sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific. The pattern tends to bring milder weather to western and Central Canada, according to the Government of Canada. The city said a longer, milder fall and slower start to winter are expected, which experts say may be intensified by climate change. Mississauga warned that freeze thaw cycles could affect outdoor rinks, trees and infrastructure. Warmer temperatures make it harder to maintain rink ice, the city said. Mississauga said it may delay the planned Nov. 21 opening of its four outdoor rinks due to safety concerns.
